title: चित्रकलेच्या माध्यमातून मध्ययुगीन आणि आधुनिक महाराष्ट्रीय समाजातील कर्तबगार महिलांचा अभ्यास
abstract: महाराष्ट्राच्या सांस्कृतिक इतिहासात चित्रकला ही केवळ सौंदर्याभिव्यक्तीची कला नसून सामाजिक स्मृती, धार्मिक अनुभव, लोकपरंपरा आणि इतिहासदृष्टी यांची दृश्यभाषा आहे. प्रस्तुत संशोधन-पत्राचा उद्देश मध्ययुगीन ते आधुनिक महाराष्ट्रीय समाजातील कर्तबगार महिलांचे स्थान चित्रकलेच्या माध्यमातून अभ्यासणे हा आहे. या अभ्यासात दोन परस्परपूरक प्रश्न विचारले आहेत: एक, चित्रांमध्ये स्त्रीचे प्रतिनिधित्व कसे घडते; आणि दोन, स्त्रिया स्वतः चित्रपरंपरेच्या सर्जक व वहनकर्त्या म्हणून कशा कार्यरत असतात. उपलब्ध दृश्यसामग्रीचा विचार करता, “मध्ययुगीन” महाराष्ट्राचा अभ्यास थेट राजदरबारी चित्रांपेक्षा आख्यानपर आणि लोकपरंपरेच्या साहाय्याने अधिक शक्य होतो; म्हणून पैठणची चित्रकाठी/रामायणपर चित्रपरंपरा, वारली चित्रकला, जिजाबाईंची आधुनिक दृश्यस्मृती आणि अंबिका धुरंधर यांसारख्या आधुनिक कलाकारांचे उदाहरण येथे केंद्रस्थानी घेतले आहे. या अभ्यासाचा मुख्य निष्कर्ष असा आहे की महाराष्ट्रीय दृश्यसंस्कृतीत स्त्री केवळ अलंकारिक प्रतिमा नाही; ती नैतिक शक्ती, सांस्कृतिक वाहक, लोककलेची सर्जक, ऐतिहासिक स्मृतीची केंद्रबिंदू आणि आधुनिक सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रातील स्वायत्त कलाकार अशा अनेक रूपांनी उपस्थित आहे. त्यामुळे चित्रकला ही कर्तबगार महिलांच्या इतिहासलेखनासाठी पूरक नव्हे, तर आवश्यक स्रोत मानली पाहिजे.

title: Ресурсный потенциал хвостов обогащения Карамкенского горно-обогатительного комбината (Магаданская область)
journal: Bulletin of the North-East Science Center
abstract: The article considers the processing tailings of gold-silver ores from the Karamken MPP as a potential technogenic deposit. Based on the analytical studies of the chemical composition and the statistical analysis of the variability of element contents relative to average values, the predicted resources of gold and silver according to the P2 category were assessed, estimated at 3.9 tons of gold and 81.8 tons of silver. It is determined that reducing the negative environmental impact in the area of the Karamken deposit requires comprehensive processing of the tailings, including the extraction of precious metals, the use of imported rock material in the upper section of the solid tailings storage facility as inert soil for reclamation, and the production of secondary material resources from the resulting processing tailings.

title: When Does Member Governance Substitute for Regulation in Consumer-Owned Utilities?
abstract: Abstract This paper asks when member governance can substitute for external regulation in consumer-owned natural monopolies. Holding quantities fixed, usage-proportional patronage refunds neutralize the transfer motive for monopoly over-pricing, shifting the welfare margin toward operating efficiency. In a principal-agent model, a cooperative board supports and monitors a risk-averse manager under a linear cost-based incentive contract. Regulation reduces the variance of realized operating costs and supports stronger incentives, but it also imposes a compliance burden and displaces the board’s own support and monitoring. Exemption therefore raises effort only when burden relief and stronger internal governance outweigh the loss of external information. Welfare dominance further requires the operating-cost gain to cover changes in effort disutility, governance costs, risk-bearing, and the social value of discretion rents. The case for exemption is therefore conditional rather than categorical and supports hybrid oversight that retains regulatory reporting, auditing, and benchmarking while relaxing behavioral constraints.

title: Variations of Gut Protistan Microbiome in Tibetan Macaques (Macaca thibetana) Across Captive, Semi-provisioned, and Wild Environments
Using Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer for teaching and learning: A survey among health professions educators
journal: Journal of the Colleges of Medicine of South Africa
abstract: Background: Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) has the potential to transform Health Professions Education (HPE), but its integration into educational practice is likely to be influenced by the knowledge, attitudes and practices of health professions educators. The aim was to assess these educators’ knowledge and awareness, attitudes and practices regarding ChatGPT. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted at a large teaching hospital using a structured questionnaire. Data were collected and analysed quantitatively to compare responses across professional groups. Results: A convenience sample of 360 healthcare professionals was recruited, comprising medical practitioners (MPs) (46.4%), health and rehabilitation sciences practitioners (HRSP) (13.3%) and nursing practitioners (NP) (40.3%). Most participants (n = 233; 64.9%) were aged 31–50 years and self-identified as female (n = 242; 67.4%). Awareness of ChatGPT was higher among MPs (98.8%) and HRSPs (95.8%), compared with NPs (65.5%). More than half of the respondents (55.3%) agreed that ChatGPT improves teaching and learning and that students should use it (54.9%), while 81.9% supported its further development. Concerns included incorrect information (63.2%), plagiarism (78.0%) and reduced independent thinking (64.5%). The current use was low (34.9%) and only 20 (19.0%) had received prior training. Most respondents reported easy access (81.7%) and requested further training (92.5%). Conclusion: Differences in knowledge, attitudes and practices exist among health professionals and may influence the integration of ChatGPT into HPE. Further research and targeted artificial intelligence (AI) literacy programmes are recommended to support its implementation. Contribution: The study provided valuable insights that could contribute to the development of AI-inclusive curricula in HPE.

title: Thermochemical Exergy as a Simulation-Based Indicator for Recycling Sustainability and Circularity Assessment Advisory: Examples for Automotive and Mass Electronics Components
abstract: Circular Economy is infused by thermodynamics: (i) achievable circularity is essentially defined by the thermodynamics of the system, implying managing material and energy quality as best as possible as defined by physics, while (ii) challenging the economics thus the viability of circularity when attempting to maintain or achieve the highest quality of materials required by modern products. Thermodynamics explains why material flows cannot be closed well, due to the creation of the economic burden of the inevitably produced residues of too low quality at all stages of the system. Obviously energy will always not be fully recovered by a circular economy system, and entropy will increase, that challenge the nett zero narrative. This paper uniquely shows the application of thermochemical exergy, derived from system process simulation models for circular economy systems, as an important indicator for evaluating and advising on recycling sustainability and circularity in the automotive and mass electronics industries. In this contribution we advanced our simulation-based digital twin for comprehensive recycling and metallurgical processes, to calculate the physical and chemical exergy of product (re)designs and compare the simulated and quantified recycling rates, exergy efficiencies, material quality, and environmental impacts to understand the best electronic circuit (re)designs. Developed within the EU Horizon Europe CIRC-UITS project, two Design for Recycling (DfR) cases show the value of the proposed thermochemical exergetic-based assessment of automotive electronic control units by Bosch and tire pressure monitoring sensors by Aumovio to assess and support eco-design activities. These two projects combine process simulation, product design, dismantling with thermochemical exergy efficiency, environmental footprints and recycling rates of automotive parts. The results show a clear correlation between dismantling and modular design, recycling rate, footprint and exergy dissipation. The thermochemically-based simulation approach for DfR provides, to our knowledge the first with this detail, a fundamental basis for design for recycling and challenges simplistic element-based recycling rate and circular economy evaluations, the present norm. A key outcome of this work shows that modules must be best designed for dismantling and harmonize with suitable metallurgical processing infrastructure. This produces the highest recycling rate while minimizing exergy dissipation as well as waste creation. This work has been recognized by European Commissions (EC) Innovation Radar's public website as innovative.

title: Succession planning in nurses leadership: Perceptions from a public hospital in Mangaung district, Free State province
journal: SA Journal of Human Resource Management
abstract: Orientation: Structured leadership succession planning is vital for maintaining management continuity in healthcare; however, such frameworks are frequently absent within the South African public hospital sector. Research purpose: The purpose of this study was to determine the perceptions and experiences of leadership succession planning for registered professional nurses in Mangaung district, Free State province. Motivation for the study: Although structured leadership transitions are vital, succession planning within public healthcare sectors continues to be predominantly informal, ad hoc and detached from organisational policy. Research approach/design and method: A qualitative research design was employed using in-depth unstructured interviews. Data were collected from 20 participants in Mangaung district and analysed using Braun and Clarke thematic analysis. Main findings: The results revealed that leadership development is commonly perceived as a secret administrative task rather than a shared professional practice. Practical/managerial implications: The findings support the need to consider succession planning that incorporates mentorship, knowledge transfer and effective communication, in line with the transformational leadership principles and best practices. Contribution/value-add: This study highlighted that a clear policy-driven succession planning is essential to enhance human resource practices, foster nurse leadership and ensure the long-term success of public health system reforms in South Africa.
